applies_why: The judge text makes an UNDERDETERMINED ruling on Romans 1:3 by citing a lack of explicit textual resolution of paternity.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: The rule phrase "a single verse does not state a link or its contrary" could mean (a) any UNDERDETERMINED based on a verse's lack of explicit textual resolution is barred, or (b) only a bare single-verse omission is barred and a whole-chain lack of resolution is allowed; the judge text falls under (a) because it cites Romans 1:3 and lack of explicit textual resolution.
why: The judge uses the lack of explicit textual resolution of paternity after weighing Romans 1:3 as the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which K-S2 forbids.
